newsitem.title: EGYPT: Egypt Shams Housing raises 95/6 dividend.
newsitem.headline: Egypt Shams Housing raises 95/6 dividend.

text.p: The Egyptian state-majority Shams Housing and Development raised cash dividends for the 95/6 financial year to 0.70 pounds from 0.40 pounds in the previous year, a company executive said on Tuesday.
Net sales, however, fell to 34.00 million pounds from 37.00 million in 94/95, the official, who asked for anonymity, told Reuters.
Distributable profits increased sharply to 13.463 million pounds ($3.96 million) from 8.07 million in 94/5, published financial statements showed.
In September, Reuters quoted sources close to the firm as saying net profits rose to 13.39 million.

The official National for Construction and Development holds 8.4 million shares of the firm's total 14 million shares. Other shareholders include state-owned Misr Insurance (25.27 percent), other institutions (8.22 percent) and individuals (6.63 percent).
The holding company had offered 74 percent, or 6.2 million shares, of its stake in Shams Housing for sale, but later refused all bids.
"The firm's capital structure remains unchanged," the official said, denying rumours that the parent company was selling its shares in Shams through brokers.
"This is not the state's policy," he said.
